a male given name from Old Norse [in turn from Latin, in turn from Ancient Greek, in turn from Biblical Hebrew], equivalent to English Matt

1001293.etyen:
Inherited from Old Norse Mats m, a short form of Mattis m, itself a Nordic form of Latin Matthias m, from Ancient Greek Ματθίας m (Matthías), ultimately from Biblical Hebrew מַתִּתְיָהוּ m (Mattīṯyāhū, “gift of Yahweh”). In Norwegian, the name is usually traced through Mathias rather than Matteus.
Compare Norwegian Nynorsk Mats, Swedish Mats, Danish Mats, Faroese Mats, Finnish Mats and Estonian Mats (“male given name”).

1001549.etyen:
PIE word
 *h₂émsus
Inherited from Old Norse Áshildr, from Proto-Germanic *Ansuhildiz, equivalent to Old Norse áss (“god; one of the Æsir”) + hildr (“battle”), literally “god-battle”.
The first element, áss (“god; one of the Æsir”), is from Proto-Germanic *ansuz (“god”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂émsus, itself from the root *h₂ems- (“to engender, beget”). The second element, hildr (“battle”), is from Proto-Germanic *hildiz (“battle, fight”); its deeper etymology is uncertain, though a derivation from Proto-Indo-European *kelh₂- (“to hit, strike”) has been proposed.
Compare Norwegian Nynorsk Å

1005133.etyen:
From gess (“G-flat”) + -ess (“semitone-lowering suffix”), literally “G-flat-flat”. The base gess (“G-flat”) is itself formed from g (“the note G”) and -ess (“semitone-lowering suffix; flat”). The suffix -ess is from German -es (“semitone-lowering suffix; flat”).
Compare the parallel formations Danish geses, Swedish gessess, German Geses, Dutch geses and Finnish geses (“G double flat”).
